content.text: [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/digital-product-stores-kyc-[[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/tron-usdt-payments-digital-products-explained-digital-creators-17|COREMERCH guide to payments]]-what-actually-how-9|Digital Product]] creators in regions with payment processing restrictions face a significant challenge: building a reliable online store. Platforms like Stripe and PayPal are often unavailable, leaving creators with no straightforward way to accept payments or manage their digital products. This guide focuses on using [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/supabase-order-database-digital-stores-step-step-deployment-17|supabase]] as an order database for your digital store, ensuring that you can set up an efficient infrastructure without relying on restricted platforms.
Why This Infrastructure Works When Platforms Fail

The current landscape of digital commerce is riddled with barriers, particularly for creators in countries where conventional payment platforms are not accessible. By leveraging infrastructure like Supabase, you bypass these limitations. Supabase offers a robust, open-source database solution that allows you to manage your orders efficiently, while NOWPayments facilitates seamless crypto transactions. This combination ensures your store operates independently, without the risk of sudden platform changes disrupting your business.
What You Need Before You Deploy

Before deploying your digital store, gather the necessary tools: a GitHub account for hosting, a Supabase account for order management, and NOWPayments to handle your crypto transactions. You will also need the Sovereign Blueprint for guidance on deployment. Ensure your digital products are ready, whether they are ebooks, courses, or templates. This preparation streamlines the process, allowing you to deploy Stack 01 efficiently within 4-6 hours.
Setting Up Your Payment and Delivery Pipeline

Begin by configuring your Supabase instance to handle order data. Set up tables for product listings, customer information, and transaction records. Next, integrate NOWPayments to enable automatic crypto payment processing. When a customer makes a purchase, the payment confirmation triggers an automated webhook that updates your Supabase database and facilitates product delivery. This workflow ensures that you maintain full control over your orders and customer data.
Supabase provides a powerful order management solution without the need for traditional payment platforms.
Going Live and Processing Your First Transaction

Once your infrastructure is in place, it's time to go live. Test your payment and delivery pipeline to ensure everything functions as expected. Make your store accessible to customers by sharing your GitHub Pages link. When your first transaction occurs, monitor the process closely. The NOWPayments integration should automatically confirm the payment and update your Supabase database in real-time. This level of automation minimizes delays and enhances the customer experience.
Scaling Once the Infrastructure Is Running

After successfully launching your digital store, consider strategies for scaling. Expand your product offerings by adding more digital items to your Supabase database. Utilize analytics to understand customer behavior and tailor your marketing efforts effectively. If you're looking for a more robust setup, consider upgrading to the Edge Commerce Stack for enhanced capabilities, including Cloudflare Workers for optimized performance and additional features. This transition can significantly improve your operational efficiency as your store grows.
How do I build a digital store that accepts crypto payments for free?

The setup sequence matters because each component depends on the previous one being correctly configured. Start with NOWPayments: create your account, configure wallet addresses for each coin you want to accept, generate the API key, and note the IPN secret key you will set. Then configure the backend: in Stack 01, deploy the Google Apps Script Web App and note its URL; in Stack 02, deploy the Cloudflare Worker and note its URL. Set that URL as the webhook endpoint in your NOWPayments IPN settings. Then configure the storefront. Then run a real mainnet test — send actual crypto to your configured wallet address, confirm NOWPayments detects it, confirm the webhook fires, and confirm the delivery email arrives with a working download link.
NOWPayments enables you to accept over 300 cryptocurrencies with minimal fees and no KYC.

Both result in the same ownership structure: your GitHub or Cloudflare account, your Supabase database, your NOWPayments account, your wallet, your store. See both options at https://coremerch.github.io/products.html.
Your Deployment Checklist

Follow the setup sequence without skipping steps — configuration errors are significantly harder to diagnose than setup time. First: create your NOWPayments account, add wallet addresses, generate your API key, and note your IPN secret key. Second: deploy the backend — configure Cloudflare Worker with your NOWPayments credentials and product settings, or configure Google Apps Script with the same — and confirm the endpoint URL. Third: set the webhook endpoint URL in your NOWPayments IPN settings. Fourth: deploy the storefront to Cloudflare Pages or GitHub Pages and confirm product pages and checkout display correctly. Fifth: configure your custom domain and DNS if using one. Sixth: complete a real mainnet test transaction. Seventh: check the order database for the test entry. Only after steps six and seven pass cleanly should you share the store URL publicly.

Yes, both GitHub Pages and Cloudflare Pages are suitable for hosting digital product stores. Choose GitHub Pages for a simpler setup or Cloudflare Pages for more advanced performance optimization options.
